implemented_scope: Native File menu and command search expose JPEG and TIFF. All three raster formats use the existing immutable owned recorder/worker path, physical DPI and Page/Content/Selection bounds, frozen full-scene routing, assigned backgrounds, group expansion and one outward pixel guard.

JPEG is a single 8-bit RGB image on fixed opaque white; partly transparent artwork composites over white. Three ImageIO quality presets request 60/85/100 percent. Maximum remains lossy. Unsupported transparency and quality on other formats refuse.

TIFF is one 8-bit RGB/alpha image using ImageIO defaults. Supported transparency or explicit white paper are retained. No multipage, compression-choice, CMYK, palette, bilevel or higher bit-depth claim is made.

Both new formats accept fractional 36–1200 DPI. Physical density is explicit TIFF X/YResolution with integer ResolutionUnit 2; for JPEG this is in EXIF TIFF-IFD0. JPEG JFIF unit 0 is square aspect ratio only. The writer does not claim absolute physical density for JFIF-only consumers.

Existing 100-million-pixel, 100,000-axis and 128 MiB retained-record caps remain; JPEG adds a conservative65,000-axis product bound. Main raster preparation and captured snapshot semantics, source/destination alias protection, cancellation/closed-owner gates and staged output preservation remain.

Actual JPEG/TIFF/PNG outputs are independently checked with Pillow and direct JPEG APP0/APP1 TIFF-IFD parsing. All 31 retained images were visually inspected through unchanged-byte-bound contact sheets; 25.4 mm one-inch and20 mm public 1:50 markers were independently measured.

regression_dispositions.observation: First 79-test run had one failure: the proposed local JFIFunit 1 assumption did not match actual ImageIO output. The file already had EXIF rational 300 DPI and ResolutionUnit 2, while JFIFunit 0 described aspect ratio. The first code also imposed whole-number JPEG DPI solely for that unsupported JFIF assumption.

Eight isolated ImageIO variants confirmed JFIF remains unit 0. An additional fractional experiment exposed Swift numeric dictionary inference: mixing rational resolutions with untyped integer literals can turn ResolutionUnit into Double, and ImageIO may omit it. Final code uses explicitly heterogeneous[CFString: Any] density with integer unit 2. Independent direct TIFF-IFD checks and fractional 300.5 DPI pixel/physical assertions replace the unsupported JFIF1 assumption. No JPEG bytes are manually patched.

Corrected 79-test focused run passes, including 20 new format tests and existing print/output/search tests. Failed/corrected files and producer experiments remain retained. Full native event-routing qualification remains pending, with no native tests excluded for acceptance.

primary_contracts.scope: JFIF1.02 page 5: density unit 0 means aspect ratio;1inches;2centimetres.
CIPA TIFF-derived image metadata: X/YResolution rational pixels per ResolutionUnit;unit 2 = inches.

limitations: All 204 M3 children and milestone remain unaccepted. No push, integration, main merge, publication or release permission is granted. M2 release exceptions are not adopted for M3.

Full current-source qualification awaits native window activation after the user dismisses the system prompt. Focused tests, skipped prerequisites, independent local decoders and saved print PDFs do not establish exact-build runtime or calibrated physical-printer acceptance.

JPEG physical DPI requires an EXIF-aware consumer; JFIF-only consumers receive square aspect ratio without absolute density. No chroma sampling/progressive/profile/file-size/fidelity guarantee. ImageIO finalization is synchronous and not interruptible; a cancellation after the existing final atomic boundary can accompany a complete file.

New commands are native UI exports. The existing headless --render-document CLI remains PNG/PDF/SVG. Full raster/vector/print/catalog and remaining M3 contracts stay open. Crops remain conservative publication bounds rather than pixel-tight ink bounds; retained limits do not bound total process RSS.
